clue.text: Footwear, Shaw said, comes from this tree

blocks.note: an open shoe held on by straps
a shaw is an old and dialect word for a small wood or thicket

explanation.surface: A shoe that George Bernard Shaw is quoted on, said to be made from some tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw looks like the playwright, but here it is the rare common noun for a copse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandalwood is a fragrant tropical tree whose scented timber is used for carving and incense.

clue.text: Lead in court encounter by arrangement

blocks.note: first meaning: on a tennis court, being one set ahead of your opponent
second meaning: a meeting secretly contrived, a trap

explanation.surface: A lawyer's opening move in court, or a meeting fixed in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests a law court, but it is the tennis court, where a player one set ahead is a set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is a rigged or contrived situation, and a player leading by one set is said to be a set up.

clue.text: Nuclear head going into the ground — close shave

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of nuclear
in electrics, earthing is connecting a circuit into the ground

explanation.surface: A nuclear warhead plunging into the earth, a narrow escape from disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a narrow escape, where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Bishop's approach is all-embracing

blocks.note: first meaning: a chess bishop moves diagonally over the chessboard
second meaning: applying to everyone or everything equally

explanation.surface: A churchman's welcoming manner takes everyone in.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is the chess piece, not a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An across-the-board measure applies universally, to every case without exception, hence all-embracing.

clue.text: Whereby some of the seeds fell out of the track team

definitions.text: Whereby some of the seeds fell

blocks.note: a way is a path or track
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Seeds falling out, alongside an athletics team at the track.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable of the sower some seeds fell by the wayside; whereby splits as where plus by.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel parable some seeds fell by the wayside, the edge of the road, where birds ate them.

clue.text: Ancient king put amateur in charge of Celtic script

blocks.note: Og was the biblical king of Bashan
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham actor or radio ham
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An old monarch puts a novice in charge of the Celtic writing system.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is the ancient Irish and Celtic alphabet of strokes, and the adjective describes anything relating to it.

clue.text: Sort of party platform that gets trimmed

indicators.note: trimming cuts a little off the end, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a stage is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A political party's platform, its policies, being cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Party platform reads as a manifesto, but party belongs to the definition and platform to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a celebration for a man before his wedding, so stag names that kind of party.

clue.text: Walk from the top of the slope

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the
a ramp is an inclined slope

explanation.surface: Setting off on a hike from the summit of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way, heavily and steadily, on foot.

clue.text: Sponsor for top garden contest

indicators.note: to contest something is to dispute it, so these letters are challenged and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A company sponsoring a prize for the best garden in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism a godparent is the sponsor who vouches for the child and promises its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Request certain Lords perhaps to provide an ornamental garden

blocks.note: a plea is an earnest request
sure means certain
Lord's is a London cricket ground, so it is one example of a ground

explanation.surface: Asking some peers in the House of Lords to fund a decorative garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords suggests peers, but read as Lord's it is the famous cricket ground in north London; perhaps marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure-ground is a landscaped park or garden laid out for enjoyment and recreation.

clue.text: Support for the service provided by brewers

definitions.text: Support for the service provided by brewers

blocks.clueFragment: Support for the service provided by brewers
blocks.note: surface reading: backing for a service run by beer makers
setter's reading: the brewers are people making a pot, and the service is the cups and saucers they carry on it

explanation.walkthrough: Brewers suggests breweries and beer, and service suggests a business; here they are tea-makers and a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board with raised edges carries the cups, saucers and pot of a set of crockery for afternoon drinks.

clue.text: Country house in Kensington

blocks.note: first meaning: the common English name for the Netherlands
second meaning: ... House is a historic mansion in Kensington, a district of west London

explanation.surface: A country house sitting in a smart London neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Country house wants to be read as a single phrase, a rural mansion; it splits after Country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is popularly called by this name, and the Jacobean Holland House stands in Holland Park, west London.

clue.text: Elemental feature at the heart of Tolkien

definitions.text: Elemental feature at the heart of Tolkien

blocks.clueFragment: Elemental feature at the heart of Tolkien
blocks.note: surface reading: a primal theme at the core of Tolkien's fantasy writing
setter's reading: the middle letter of the name is K, the chemical symbol of an element

explanation.surface: A literary critic finding something primal at the core of Tolkien's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Elemental sounds like primal forces in Middle-earth; it means a chemical element, and the heart of Tolkien is its central letter, K.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol for this soft alkali metal, from its Latin name kalium.

clue.text: Mountain hospital gets a good mark

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alpine hospital earns a good rating from inspectors.
explanation.definitionFit: In British grading, an alpha is a top mark for school or university work, the highest grade.

clue.text: Short-lived writer

blocks.note: first meaning: brief, over quickly
second meaning: Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: An author who died young.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief passes quickly, and Jonathan Swift was the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: “Bright star, would I were — as thou art” (Keats)

definitions.text: “Bright star, would I were — as thou art” (Keats)

blocks.clueFragment: “Bright star, would I were — as thou art”
blocks.note: surface reading: the opening line of a Keats sonnet with one word missing
setter's reading: the word Keats used for the star is the answer, in its modern spelling

explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Keats's sonnet Bright Star opens with the poet wishing he were as constant as the star.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet wishes he were as unchanging and constant as the fixed star, which never moves in the sky.

clue.text: In a frenzy, urge canoe forward

indicators.note: a frenzy is a wild, disordered state, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic paddler driving a canoe onward.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward reads as a direction, but it is the verb meaning to promote or help along.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a cause is to promote or help it along, which is what support and urging do.

clue.text: Forest feature enough to make a Simian scratch its head

definitions.text: Forest feature enough to make a Simian scratch its head

blocks.clueFragment: Forest feature enough to make a Simian scratch its head
blocks.note: surface reading: something in the woods that would baffle an ape

blocks.clueFragment: make a Simian scratch its head
blocks.note: setter's reading: a thing that puzzles a monkey, which is the popular name of this tree

explanation.walkthrough: A thing that would puzzle a monkey is a monkey puzzle, the common name of this spiky conifer; it is also the pen-name of a famous Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey puzzle tree, with sharp overlapping leaves, belongs to this botanical genus of South American conifers.

clue.text: Helicopter a threat to such as Humpty-Dumpty

definitions.text: a threat to such as Humpty-Dumpty

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a helicopter, from its whirling blades

blocks.clueFragment: a threat to such as Humpty-Dumpty
blocks.note: second meaning: a kitchen whisk is dangerous to anything that is an egg, like the nursery-rhyme character

explanation.surface: A helicopter menacing a nursery-rhyme figure sitting on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty-Dumpty is an egg in the nursery rhyme, so a kitchen whisk would do him harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang names a chopper after a rotary kitchen whisk, and a whisk beats eggs, Humpty's kind.

clue.text: Tour-de-force — ruff when holding one heart

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: in card games to ruff is to play a trump
the Roman numeral for one
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card notation

explanation.surface: A masterly bridge play: trumping while still holding a single heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The card words ruff and heart keep the whole surface at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour de force is an outstanding achievement or feat of skill, which is a great success.

clue.text: In Paris street you get English money for train

indicators.note: in places the following words inside the street name, so they sit within it

blocks.note: rue is French for street, as in Paris
E is the abbreviation for English
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A tourist in a Paris street changing English currency for a rail ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like the railway, but it means a following, like a monarch's attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a procession of followers or attendants, the people who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Eastern treaty in the satellite age

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
a pact is a treaty or formal agreement

explanation.surface: An Eastern-bloc treaty signed in the space era of satellites.
explanation.walkthrough: The satellite age sounds like the space era; the satellite is the Moon, and its age is counted in days.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the Moon's age in days at the start of the year, used for calculating Easter.

clue.text: Athenian statesman to look up to?

blocks.note: first meaning: the lawgiver of ancient Athens, famous for harsh laws
second meaning: a constellation of the northern sky, which you see by gazing upward

explanation.surface: An ancient Athenian politician worthy of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: To look up to suggests admiring someone, which suits the statesman; read literally it is something in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian lawgiver behind draconian laws, and Draco the Dragon is a northern constellation.

clue.text: A puzzle to surprise

blocks.note: taken as written
a maze is a puzzle of paths

explanation.surface: A brain-teaser designed to catch people off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to catch them completely off guard, the strongest kind of shock.

clue.text: Programmed trains etc to give rest times

definitions.note: noun: interacts are intervals between the acts of a play

indicators.note: something programmed is set out in a new sequence, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rail timetable programmed to give staff their breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Interacts looks like a verb, but here it is the plural noun for the intervals between acts in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An interact is an interval in the theatre, a pause between acts when audience and players get a break.

clue.text: Determine to clear up after the soldiers leave

indicators.note: once the troops depart they are no longer present, so their letters are dropped

blocks.note: to resolve a matter is to clear it up
RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers

explanation.surface: Resolving to tidy up the barracks once the troops have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Determine to reads as resolve to, a natural phrase, but determine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine an answer is to work it out, settling a problem or question.

clue.text: Able to go to Elba, for example

definitions.text: Able to go to Elba, for example

blocks.note: surface reading: someone fit to travel to Napoleon's island
setter's reading: the word able reshuffled spells the island's name, which is an instance of a wordplay device

explanation.surface: Someone well enough to travel to the island of Elba.
explanation.walkthrough: Able looks like an adjective meaning fit, but it is a word whose letters rearrange to spell Elba.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of able produces Elba, a textbook instance of the letter-rearranging device crosswords use.

clue.text: Not engaged, just sitting on the fence

blocks.note: first meaning: a car's gear position with no gear engaged
second meaning: taking no side in a dispute

explanation.surface: An unattached person content to stay undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: Not engaged suggests not betrothed; it is the gearbox position where no gear meshes.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gear where the engine drives nothing, and a neutral party takes no side.

clue.text: Elder Thespian

blocks.note: first meaning: the elder is a small ... with white flowers and dark berries
second meaning: Sir Herbert Beerbohm ..., the Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.walkthrough: Elder suggests an older person, perhaps a senior actor; it is the shrub with elderberries.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a species of small tree, and Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated English actor.

clue.text: Worn-out, like Theseus before Ariadne aided him

definitions.text: like Theseus before Ariadne aided him

blocks.note: first meaning: shabby, with the nap rubbed away

blocks.clueFragment: like Theseus before Ariadne aided him
blocks.note: second meaning: without any string, since Ariadne gave the hero a ball of it to find his way out of the Labyrinth

explanation.surface: A weary Greek hero, exhausted until a princess came to help.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Greek myth Ariadne gave Theseus a clue of yarn to escape the Minotaur's maze; before that he had none.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is shabby from wear, and split as thread plus bare it means lacking string.
